record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.context_brief: Embedding a linear functional equation into continuous time
record.original_question: Given the linear functional equation φ(f(x)) = g(x)φ(x) + h(x), determine weak assumptions on the data f, g, and h that allow this equation to be embedded into a continuous-time family φ(F(t,x)) = G(t,x)φ(x) + H(t,x), where F, G, and H satisfy the semigroup and cocycle relations listed in the paper, match f, g, h at time t=1, and are such that every solution of the discrete-time equation also satisfies the continuous-time one.

evidence.quote: The following problem concerning the linear equation ϕ(f(x)) = g(x)ϕ(x) + h(x) (10.5) was posed by L. Reich [213]. He asked under what possibly weak assumptions on the given functions f, g, h we can ‘embed’ (10.5) in the equation with ‘continuous time’ argument: ϕ(F(t, x)) = G(t, x)ϕ(x) + H(t, x).

More precisely: under what assumptions on f, g, h there exist F, G, H from a suitable class of functions solving equations F(t + s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)), G(t + s, x) = G(s, x)G(t, F(s, x)), H(t + s, x) = G(t, F(s, x))H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x)) and fulfilling conditions F(1, ·) = f, G(0, ·)=1, G(1, ·) = g, H(0, ·)=0, H(1, ·) = h such that every solution of (10.5) from the considered function class satisfies equation (10.6).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the linear functional equation in a single unknown function φ:
    φ(f(x)) = g(x) φ(x) + h(x),    (*)
where f, g, h are given functions on a set X (with f: X → X and g, h: X → ℝ or ℂ), and the unknown φ is sought in some specified function class.

One says that (*) can be embedded in a continuous-time linear functional equation if there exist functions F, G, H defined on [0,∞) × X such that:

(i) (Semigroup / cocycle relations) for all t, s ≥ 0 and all x ∈ X,
        F(t+s, x) = F(t, F(s, x)),
        G(t+s, x) = G(s, x) · G(t, F(s, x)),
        H(t+s, x) = G(t, F(s, x)) · H(s, x) + H(t, F(s, x));

(ii) (Initial and matching conditions)
        F(1, ·) = f,    G(0, ·) = 1,    G(1, ·) = g,    H(0, ·) = 0,    H(1, ·) = h;

(iii) (Compatibility of solutions) every φ in the considered function class which solves (*) also satisfies the continuous-time equation
        φ(F(t, x)) = G(t, x) φ(x) + H(t, x)    for all t ≥ 0 and x ∈ X.

Problem. Determine the weakest possible assumptions on the data f, g, h (and on the underlying function class) under which such an embedding (F, G, H) exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is attributed to L. Reich and is described as an open problem in a recent survey on functional equations in a single variable. Web search did not surface a published solution; the problem appears to remain open.
